gaps.message: Building Control (/default.asp): navigation to the page — Discovery reached this page by its address (a listed route, the sitemap or the start page), not by clicking, so no click path is known.
journeys across several forms — End-to-end workflows are taken from recorded journeys. They are not inferred from discovery, because the order of real business steps is not visible in the page.
a scan scoped to the form — The form has no selector the scanner can be scoped with, so the whole page is scanned.
a scan scoped to the form — The form has no selector the scanner can be scoped with, so the whole page is scanned.

authorization, access control and object references — Who may submit this form, and with whose records, is a property of the account, not the page; it is tested at application level by the security engine against its scope.

authorization, access control and object references — Who may submit this form, and with whose records, is a property of the account, not the page; it is tested at application level by the security engine against its scope.
server-side validation — The browser's own validation stops an invalid submission before it reaches the server, so whether the server checks too cannot be seen from the page.
server-side validation — The browser's own validation stops an invalid submission before it reaches the server, so whether the server checks too cannot be seen from the page.
server timeouts and authorization errors — A timeout or a 401/403 cannot be provoked from the page without changing the server.
server timeouts and authorization errors — A timeout or a 401/403 cannot be provoked from the page without changing the server.

business rules between fields beyond those named — Rules such as "business accounts need a company number" exist in requirements, not in the page; only rules visible in names or observed in behaviour were tested.
the stored record — QA NXT has no access to the application's database, and a stored record is only observable where the application shows it back.
load, stress, spike and endurance testing — These need many concurrent virtual users over time. The browser worker measures single-user response times; it is not a load generator.
a network failure during submission — This form submits by navigating, so a network failure is shown by the browser's own error page, not by the application.
